items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a weakly etale ring map A -> B and asserts that if A has weak dimension at most d then so does B (source lines 30230-30234). The proof is a resolution argument split by the value of d. Let N be a B-module. If d = 0, then N is flat as an A-module, hence flat as a B-module by the key lemma (proof lines 30237-30238). Assume d > 0: choose a resolution F_bullet -> N by free B-modules (proof lines 30239-30240). The hypothesis on A implies that the image K of F_d -> F_{d-1} is A-flat, by the last-term-flat statement (proof lines 30240-30242). Hence K is B-flat by the key lemma (proof lines 30242-30243). Then 0 -> K -> F_{d-1} -> ... -> F_0 -> N -> 0 is a flat resolution of length d, so N has tor dimension at most d (proof lines 30244-30246). The non-routine content is the choice of the truncation point: the syzygy at position d is A-flat by the weak dimension hypothesis, and weak etaleness of A -> B, used through the key lemma, upgrades that A-flatness to B-flatness.
